description.narrative: Denna insats avser stöd till FNs migrationsorganisation, IOM, för genomförande av den andra fasen av projekt We Belong under treårsperioden 2024-2026. Den totala budgeten uppgår till trettio miljoner SEK, Sida är enda givare och projektet genomförs av the Office of the Director Generals Special Envoy for the Regional Response to the Venezuela Situation (OCE) med säte i Panama. Projektets övergripande mål är att bidra till hållbar integration av migranter genom en insats med brett fokus som innefattar ökade möjligheter till sysselsättning, stöd till entreprenörer och småföretagare samt stärkt kapacitet hos lokala myndigheter och civilsamhället för att främja socioekonomisk integration av migranter. De planerade aktiviteterna är organiserade kring tre komponenter: 1. Migranters ökade möjligheter till anställning Genom projektet kommer migranter att få ökade möjligheter till anställning med anständiga villkor i sektorer som har identifierats som växande och som idag har stora behov av arbetskraft. Föreslagna sektorer är inom så kallade gröna jobb, turism samt IT-sektorn. Projektet kommer även att bidra till en mer gynnsam politik för migranters möjlighet till anställning. Studier kommer att tas fram för att belysa migranternas betydelse för ekonomisk utveckling, dessa kommer sen att ligga till grund för påverkansarbete och kampanjer för en mer inkluderande arbetsmarknadspolitik i regionen. 2. Stöd till entreprenörer Projektet kommer att stödja mikro-, små och medelstora företag, som ägs av migranter och/eller personer i värdsamhällena, för att dessa ska kunna expandera och skapa sysselsättningsmöjligheter för både migranter och medlemmar av värdsamhällena. Nyckelaktiviteter är inledande pilotverksamhet inom IOM:s företagsutvecklingsfond (Enterprise Development Fund) och entreprenörers tillgång till regionala handelsmässor. 3. Lokala myndigheter och civilsamhällets ökade kapacitet att främja integation För att stärka migrationshantering och migranters möjlighet att delta i utformning av policies för integration kommer projektet att stödja genomförandet av rekommendationer som härrör från IOM:s Migration Government Indicators. Detta innefattar stöd till lokalt identifierade projekt för att stärka socioekonomisk integration. Dessutom kommer projektet att stödja aktiviteter för att öka kapaciteten hos aktörer inom civilsamhället genom att främja dialoger och utbyte mellan organisationer samt möjligheter att konkret stödja integration av migranter. Slutligen kommer IOM att fortsätta stöd till Quitoprocessen, särskilt pro-tempore ordförandeskapet och de tekniska arbetsgrupperna, med tonvikt på arbetsgruppen för socioekonomisk integration och därmed stödja genomförandet av den regionala strategin för socioekonomiska integration av migranter från Venezuela som samordnas av ILO och UNDP. Projektet kommer huvudsakligen att genomföras i Aruba, Argentina, Brasilien, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador och Panama. Den geografiska täckningen kan förändras och kommer slutgiltigt att baserat på i vilken grad integration prioriteras i länderna och annan lokal dynamik i Latinamerika och Karibien.

This contribution concerns support to the second phase of IOM's project We Belong during the three-year period 2024-2026. The total budget amounts to 30 million SEK, Sida is the only donor, and the project is implemented by the Office of the Director Generals Special Envoy for the Regional Response to the Venezuela Situation (OCE) situated in Panama.
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to sustainable migrant integration through a comprehensive intervention that focuses on Access to Employment; Entrepreneurship Support; and Capacity Strengthening of Local Authorities and Civil Society.
The planned activities are organized around three main components:
1. Promote access to Employment: The project aims to facilitate migrants' access to formal and decent employment opportunities in sectors that have been identified as growing and that currently have high labour demands. Proposed sectors are so called green jobs, tourism, information and communication technology (ICT). Moreover, the project will contribute to more favourable policies for migrant employment, e.g. studies will be produced to highlight the importance of migrants in the development process, and these will be the basis for advocacy efforts and dissemination campaigns towards more inclusive labour policies in the region.
2. Entrepreneurship Support: The project will support micro, small and medium enterprises, owned and/or managed by migrants and/or members of the host communities, to expand and generate employment opportunities for both migrants and members of the host communities. More specifically, IOM will implement two key activities: a) IOM's Enterprise Development Fund, and b) Access to Regional Trade Fairs.
3. Capacity strengthening of local authorities and civil society: In order to strengthen participation and migration governance, the project will support governments in implementing recommendations stemming from IOM's Migration Government Indicators and local integration projects identified through participatory planning processes. This will be done in collaboration and/or partnership with the Organization of American States (OAS) and the Latin American Federation of Cities, Municipalities and Local Government Associations (FLACMA, by its Spanish acronym). In addition, capacity building activities will target civil society actors, by promoting dialogues and exchanges between Civil Society Organizations as well as providing in-kind support to strengthen their capacities to provide integration support to migrants. Lastly, IOM will ensure linkages between the proposed initiatives and the Quito Process, through continued general coordination support to the Pro-Tempore Presidency and the technical working groups, with emphasis to the Socio-economic Integration Working Group, ensuring the promotion of the Regional Socioeconomic Integration Strategy.
Potential target countries are Aruba, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Panama. The geographical coverage will be finally determined based on integration priorities and local dynamics in Latin America and the Caribbean.

The overall objective of the second phase of the project We Belong, implemented by IOM, is to contribute to sustainable migrant integration through a comprehensive intervention that focuses on i) Access to Employment ii) Entrepreneurship Support and iii) Capacity Strengthening of Local Authorities and Civil Society.
The project has three outcome goals:
1 Economic integration of migrants is strengthened through more comprehensive and effective multilevel activities towards private sector sensitation and increment of migrants' employablity. Two outputs will contribute to the first outcome goal: 1.1 Local authorities and employers improved perceptions of migrants and awareness of migrant contributions to the local economy results in greater openness to integrate migrants. 1.2 Private Sector enterprises are better able to promote migrant employment due to their access to necessary information and guidance, such as on recruitment procedures, existing best practices and recommendations to address obstacles.
2. Migrants are able to generate income as a result of improved entrepreneurship opportunities. Two outputs will contribute to the second outcome goal: 2.1 Migrants have the knowledge and capacities to start up or strengthen their own businesses. 2.2 Migrants are better integrated in local and regional entrepreneurial environments promoting their business growth.
3. Civil society and local authorities are strengthened to better address integration needs of migrants Three outputs will contribute to the third outcome goal: 3.1 Civil society has the needed knowledge and resources to design relevant integration programs and strategies. 3.2 Venezuelan CSOs, with greater focus on CSOs led by Venezuelan women, have the capacities to voice their issues and advocate effectively on integration needs and priorities in local, national, regional, and global forums. 3.3 Local authorities and communities have the needed knowledge and resources to design and implement relevant integration programs and strategies based on community based planning.

description.narrative:
2024
Below are examples of activities and results, during the first year of project implementation, related to each of the outcome objectives for the project.
1. Migrants are better integrated socially and economically in their host communities. Study on the fiscal and economic contribution of Venezuelan migration in Peru: To improve local authorities and employers perceptions of migrants contributions to the local economies and increase the openness to integrate migrants, IOM has continued to produce studies to evidence the extent to which migrants contribute economically to host local communities. In 2024 an Analysis of the Fiscal and Economic Contribution of Venezuelan Migration in Peru was produced and disseminated. The studies findings were published at a pivotal time, highlighting the positive impact of migrants, when a new migration regularization process was being developed.
Partnerships with companies to facilitate migrants employment and fill labor market gaps: A pilot to enhance the private sectors willingness and ability to employ migrants was carried out in Ecuador. IOM, together with the Chamber of Innovation and Technology, conducted a survey among technology companies to identify labormarket gaps. Two profiles were highlighted by employers: specialized technology salespersons and digital marketing specialists. IOM then launched a program with relevant theoretical and practical training through partnerships with enterprises. After training, the participants received three months basic salary from IOM, with the aim of facilitating their employment and encouraging their retention in the participating companies. Upon completion of the initiative the goal is to train 50 people and achieve permanent employment for 20 of them.
Other planned activities contributing to this result in 2024 were delayed and carried over to 2025.
2. Migrants are able to generate income as a result of improved entrepreneurship opportunities. Job creation through the Enterprise Development Fund: The Enterprise Development Fund (EDF) methodology developed by IOM has been adapted for implementation in Latin America. In a pilot test in Ecuador 18 companies were provided grants and advisory services from IOM allowing them to expand their businesses, create new work areas and hire new staff. This led to the creation of 92 jobs with a joint investment from IOM and PRM (The US Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration) of USD 400,000. The companies signed a commitment to sustain the jobs created for six months. Based on this performance, the German Investment Bank (KFW) has decided to contribute EUR 24,000,000 to IOM Ecuador to continue strengthening the small and medium enterprise sector. Expanding upon the positive results of the Enterprise Development Fund initiative in Ecuador, IOM will disseminate the knowledge and experiences the EDF mechanism in the Americas to facilitate increased investment of diverse donors and private sector in the EDF.
Summit of the Chambers of Venezuelan Businessmen and Entrepreneurs Abroad (CAVEX): On March 5, 2024, the First Continental Summit of the Chambers of Venezuelan Businessmen and Entrepreneurs Abroad (CAVEX) was held in Panama City, with over 100 participants from all the chambers that comprise CAVEX in the Americas as well as prominent Venezuelan businessmen and entrepreneurs from Panama, Aruba, and Colombia. The summit included a dialogue with civil society through the Red Clamor and the Coalition for Venezuela resulting in a letter of intent for cooperation between the private sector and civil society in projects aimed at the protection and integration of migrants. Additionally, studies on the employability and economic contribution of Venezuelan migration in Dominican Republic and Panama, conducted by IOM and CAVEX, were presented. The event marked a significant step in raising the visibility of the private sector led by Venezuelan migrants across the region.
Networking for commercial opportunities during "Connect and Entrepreneur Southern Cone": The first "Connect and Entrepreneur Southern Cone" event was held on October 18, 2024, in Argentina with the objective to create a networking space and connections with the Venezuelan Business and Entrepreneur Chambers to explore commercial opportunities in the Southern Cone. Promising contacts were established that might lead to potential import and export lines for small business owners from Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay. Another example is that a municipality in Uruguay plans to replicate the Migrant Fair held in Buenos Aires. The event was attended by 80 people in person, while 200 people followed a virtual broadcast.
Venezuelan entrepreneurs participating in the trade fair Expocruz 2024: IOM supported part of the costs for 20 Venezuelan entrepreneurs participation in the trade fair Expocruz 2024 in Bolivia. The participating entrepreneurs report new alliances and increased sales that might lead to new employment opportunities. Eighteen participants reported making over 800 business contacts, of which more than 100 could turn into secure deals besides the sales of approximately USD 15,000 during the fair. Nine of them received quotation requests for future sales. In addition, the Venezuelan entrepreneur companies participated in business rounds generating 134 meetings over three days. A followup survey six month after the Tade Fair will provide more informetion on concrete results for the participating entrepreneurs. The IOM stand was the largest in the International Pabellon and was honored with the Sustainable Development Award. After being dismantled, it was processed and converted into cardboard boxes for commercial reuse. During the trade fair 112 videos created by a Venezuelan influencer were broadcasted under the hashtag the good ones are more sharing success stories of Venezuelans worldwide.
3. Civil society and local authorities are strengthened to better address integration needs of migrants. Migrant NGOs supported through a best practices competition: IOM conducted the IV edition of the Best Practices competition for migrant NGOs at the regional level. The three categories were: Integration, Diversity, and Inclusion Integration through Culture and Sports and Capacity Building for Entrepreneurs and Promotion of Employability. Six initiatives from Colombia, Peru, Costa Rica, Argentina, Bolivia, and Ecuador were selected among 84 proposals and the winners receive 5,000 USD each to continue to implement their good practices. The quality of the best practises presented was significantly higher then previous years and this is interpreted as a result of the support to the migrant NGOs for organizational development and strengthening of capacities for e.g design of project proposals.
Women Diaspora Leaders strengthen capacities and networking: The 3rd Regional Meeting of Diaspora Leaders joined 35 women migrant leaders in Colombia for three days in August 2024. The event was co-organized with the ILO, OAS, and the Network of Venezuelan Diaspora Leaders and for the first time included diaspora leaders both from Venezuela and other countries in the region. The leaders shared best practices, reieved training in communication and project development, and discussed topics such as combating human trafficking and xenophobia, and fund raising. The event highlighted the significant growth and maturity of the Network of Venezuelan Diaspora Leaders, which was established during the first meeting in 2022, and the important potential for growth through dialogue with other diasporas.
The Coalition for Venezuela celebrated its IV Annual Assembly: The Coalition for Venezuela received financial support from the project We Belong for its VI Annual Assembly held in Brazil in October 2024. 106 Venezuelan diaspora organization from 23 countries attended, demonstrating the coordination power of the Venezuelan diaspora. The event emphasized the importance of improving horizontal dialogues and participants exchanged experiences and knowledge of best practices and lessons learned in their work to promote rights and intergration of Venezuelan migrants and refugees. The need to cocreate innovative strategies to address the challenges faced by migrants and refugees was highlighted, along with the importance of strengthening strategic alliances by fostering partnerships between NGOs and other stakeholders. The assembly also celebrated its annual democratic elections of governing authorities and advanced the coalitions' strategic planning.
Implementation of integration projects based on communitybased planning delayed: In the first phase of the project We Belong, IOM initiated the work with community based planning to strengthen capacities and provide resources to design and implement integration programs and strategies at local level in Colombia, Panama, Ecuador, Argentina and the Dominican Republic. The communities that will carry out the local integration projects have been selected and the local authorities and communities have created spaces for communication and participatory involvement and carried out community consultations to identify issues of interest to the population. Selected projects focus on jointly identified needs and include e.g. minor infrastructure improvements such as parks and sports facilities, cultural activities and in one case the development of climate change adaptation strategies. In parallel local authorities have received training on participatory planning processes. However, electoral processes and changes in authorities, and in the case of Panama a prolonged strike in the construction sector, has delayed the processes and several projects are still in the planning phase.
Support to the Quito Process: IOM, in coordination with UNHCR, serve as technical secretariat to the Quito Process and prepared the X Plenary Meeting of the member states of the Quito Process in Costa Rica in November 2024. One of the results of the Chapter X is the commitment to continue to strengthen the Regional Mechanism to Combat Trafficking in Persons by putting into practice the Protocol on Consular Assistance and deepen the axes of relocation and prosecution. During the Plenary Meeting Guatemala was added as a member state. Paraguay, the Dominican Republic, and Argentina did not sign the final declaration but confirmed their support for the process and its continuity. Ecuador has taken over the presidency for Chapter XI and IOM continue supporting as technical secretariat.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
